questions.q: According to this lesson, what is log shipping's real, current use case?
options: Replacing Availability Groups entirely in every scenario
Real-time, zero-latency failover for mission-critical production systems
It has no legitimate current use case at all
A simple offsite reporting or DR copy where a few minutes of staleness is genuinely acceptable, especially across long distances
questions.explain: Log shipping's simplicity and tolerance for geographic distance make it a legitimate fit when some staleness is acceptable.

questions.q: Why does log shipping not require the low-latency networking that synchronous AG replication does?
options: It doesn't actually move any data between servers
Its jobs run independently on their own schedules rather than continuously streaming changes in real time
It only works on a single server with no network involved
It uses a faster network protocol than AGs do
questions.explain: Because backup/copy/restore run on independent schedules, log shipping tolerates network conditions that would be impractical for synchronous replication.

questions.q: What is the honest verdict on database mirroring, according to this lesson?
options: It should be the first choice for any new HA requirement
It should be combined with every new Availability Group deployment
It's identical to log shipping in every relevant respect
There's no 'choose it' scenario for new deployments — only a 'found it, plan to migrate it' scenario
questions.explain: Mirroring is deprecated with a mature replacement (AGs) already in place; the realistic task is migrating off it, not choosing it.

questions.q: What role do Availability Groups play in this lesson's overall framing?
options: A technology with no real relationship to log shipping or mirroring
A legacy technology being phased out in favor of mirroring
The modern default for most new HA/DR requirements, and the landing point mirroring should be migrated toward
Something only relevant to cloud-only deployments
questions.explain: AGs are positioned as the modern default and the direction mirroring deployments should move toward over time.

questions.q: A stakeholder asks whether to set up new database mirroring for an offsite reporting copy. What's the honest answer, per this lesson?
options: No — recommend log shipping or an Availability Group instead, since mirroring is deprecated with no new-deployment scenario
Mirroring should be set up first, then migrated to log shipping later
Yes, mirroring is the best choice for any offsite reporting copy
It doesn't matter; mirroring and log shipping are functionally identical
questions.explain: Given mirroring's deprecated status, the honest recommendation is log shipping (if staleness tolerance fits) or an AG, not new mirroring.
